note: Every place engine or adapter code fakes something to fit a contract. A shim means the contract does not count as used by that engine class (decision rule). Written by hand from the code; the verdict script reads it.

shims.what: HTTP is dressed as a byte stream: one Transport instance per request/response exchange; open() connects nothing (connection failures surface at write()); write() is a whole POST body; onClose() means end of response; the HTTP status is invisible through the contract; Endpoint gained path and headers only for this.
decoder() returns the identity function: bun:sqlite binds and returns JS values (bigint with safeIntegers) itself, so the registry only wraps values.
ConnectContext.transport is undefined for the service engine although a transport exists: the ServiceCore owns it, so the capability model cannot read TransportCaps for a service.

consideredNotShims.item: MySQL family: encode(startup) writes no bytes
consideredNotShims.why: The server speaks first. Contract revision R3 added the `send` event and allows encode() to produce no bytes; the contract was changed to admit it, not faked.
Contract revision R5 added the probe; real use, on the error path only.

consideredNotShims.item: MySQL family core sends COM_PING after an ERR packet to learn the transaction state
consideredNotShims.why: Engine-internal protocol work that fills observedTx; no platform contract is bypassed. Cold path only.

consideredNotShims.item: sqlite and libsql ErrorMapper: retry is the constant 'never'
consideredNotShims.why: A real answer for the one error classified; no retryable class was exercised, so this is untested rather than faked.
